Outputs: results*.json and run_base.txt. Jamal's roster is ASSUMED from the last known state (Sept 23): QB Purdy, Murray; RB Chase Brown, Kyren Williams, Jadarian Price, Emanuel Wilson; WR Nacua, Pickens, Tate, Vele, Wicks, Doubs; TE Fannin, Pitts; DST 49ers.

(1) Points-per-game curve. I took 2026 Weeks 1-6 nflverse actual PPR points per game, with QBs rescored to 6-pt passing TDs, for players with at least 3 games. I ranked them within position and fit ppg = a + b*ln(rank):
- QB: 33.39 - 5.27 ln r (R2 0.85)
- RB: 31.75 - 6.57 ln r (R2 0.98)
- WR: 29.04 - 5.16 ln r (R2 0.98)
- TE: 21.11 - 4.19 ln r (R2 0.99)

(2) Player ROS ppg. Each player gets 50% curve value at their FantasyPros ROS positional ECR (scraped Oct 16) plus 50% their own Weeks 1-6 expected points per game from ep.csv (QB passing TDs rescored to 6 points). Overrides:
- Tate is capped at 9.0.
- McLaurin is set to 0: torn patellar tendon, season over (ESPN/NFL.com, Oct 20). His Oct 16 ECR is stale.
- Tyson is 0 through Week 9. He has been on IR since Aug 30, is not practicing in Week 7, his 21-day practice window has not opened, NO is on bye in Week 8, and analysts' earliest debut is Week 9. In the model he debuts Week 10 at 60%, then plays at curve(WR36) = 10.53 ppg. That is a low-end fantasy WR3, a little below the 11.6 actual / 12.8 EP ppg that Vele has produced in the NO WR2 role Tyson was drafted for. The discount reflects rookie ramp-up and his history of hamstring recurrences.

(3) Byes come from games.csv: LA 11, SEA 11, CLE 11, ATL 11, NE 11, DAL 14, ARI 14, NO 8, SF 8, TEN 9, PHI 10. Week 11 is a hole for HOLD (Nacua, Kyren and both TEs on bye). Week 14, the last regular-season week, is a hole for every Javonte/M. Wilson option, because Pickens, Javonte and Wilson are all on bye.

(4) Lineups. Each week 8-17, the best legal QB/2RB/2WR/TE/2FLEX lineup is picked greedily, which is optimal for nested slots. DST is the same 49ers unit in every option, so it is excluded. Week 7 is excluded: the task window starts at Week 8, and the trade most likely processes after Week 7 kickoffs. Every roster, HOLD included, can use one replacement-level free agent per position each week. Replacement levels are computed on the same blended basis at QB20/RB45/WR55/TE16: QB 18.07, RB 7.53, WR 8.60, TE 9.31.

(5) Drops. These are chosen by brute force as the set that costs the fewest lineup points over Weeks 8-17, with ties going to the lowest ppg:
- 3-for-1 options (a), (b) and the extra Likely option: drop Jadarian Price and Kyle Pitts.
- (g): drop Price and McLaurin.
- 2-for-1 options: drop Price.
- Modeled cost is 0.0 points in every case. Price, Pitts, Doubs, Wicks and Kyler Murray all project at or below the free-agent streamer, so the model is indifferent among them.
- Emanuel Wilson should NOT be dropped. He is a regular FLEX starter (10.15 ppg).
- If Jamal has an open ESPN IR slot, Tyson or McLaurin could go there, saving one drop at no modeled cost.

(6) Nacua scenarios count calendar weeks missed starting with Week 7. N=1 means he is out Week 7 only and back Week 8. Every trade option is unaffected by Nacua's health, so only HOLD changes between scenarios. The 'most likely' row is a probability-weighted mix: 1 week 45%, 2 weeks 30%, 4 weeks 15%, 6 weeks 6%, 10 weeks 4%. These weights are my judgment from the evidence, not a sourced forecast:
- He was limited, not DNP, on Thursday Oct 22 (ESPN, OC Register).
- No MRI or severity has been reported, and no Friday designation was found.
- Early reads were Rotoworld 'highly questionable' and SI 'very questionable' for Week 7.
- 4for4's historical benchmark is about 2 missed weeks for WR calf strains.
- The tail risk comes from the pre-hernia/surgery talk (Florio, Schefter, Newsweek, early Oct).

Sensitivity runs:
- A waiver fill only for empty slots, or no waivers at all, both make (a) look 3-8 points better.
- M. Wilson at curve only (13.11) or at 12.0.
- Nacua at 25.0.
- Javonte at 15.0.
- Tyson returning Week 9, or Week 12 at WR45.

Known biases:
- The curve is built from rank-ordered actual results after only 6 weeks, which inflates the top ranks (helps Nacua, Olave and Cook). The EP blend partly offsets this.
- The ECR predates Week 6, McLaurin's injury and Nacua's calf injury.
- The model uses means only. It ignores Nacua's ceiling, injury risk to the incoming players, Tyson cutting into Vele's role, Corum's value as Kyren's handcuff, and the NFL's off-field review of Nacua (no timeline, no suspension).

valued.breakeven:
Base model: option (a) beats HOLD over Weeks 8-17 once Nacua misses 2 or more weeks counting Week 7, meaning he also misses Week 8.
- N=1: -1.9 pts total. That is +0.13 per week in Weeks 8-14 and -0.94 per week in Weeks 15-17.
- N=2: +12.3 pts.
- N=3: +26.2 pts.
- N=4: +40.1 pts.

In probability terms, (a) has the higher expected value if the chance he also misses Week 8 is above about 14% (1.93 / (1.93 + 12.28)).

For the playoffs alone (Weeks 15-17), (a) wins only if Nacua is still out in Week 15 (N of 9 or more). Otherwise HOLD is 2.8 points better across the three playoff weeks.

The breakeven depends on the inputs, and M. Wilson matters most:
- M. Wilson at his ECR curve value only (13.1 ppg instead of 15.2): breakeven is 3 weeks, and the probability-weighted delta is -2.6 pts.
- M. Wilson at 12.0, close to his 11.9 actual: breakeven is 4 weeks, delta -12.6.
- Nacua at 25 ppg: breakeven 3 weeks.
- Javonte at 15 ppg: breakeven 3 weeks.
- With waivers allowed only for empty slots, or no waivers at all: breakeven 1 week.

The model does not cover Week 7. The trade will likely process after kickoffs, so Week 7 is lost either way if Nacua sits.
valued.recommendation:
Don't accept yet, and don't spend the counter on Corum, McLaurin or a 2-for-1. Those are equal to or worse than the offer for Jamal.

As offered, the trade is roughly break-even if Nacua is back for Week 8:
- -1.9 pts over Weeks 8-17.
- +0.1 per week in the rest of the regular season.
- -0.9 per week in the playoffs.

It only clearly wins if he also misses Week 8: +12 pts at 2 weeks missed, +40 at 4 weeks. Weighted by my injury probabilities it is worth +16.5 pts (+2.6 per week in Weeks 8-14, -0.6 per week in Weeks 15-17). That edge disappears (-2.6) if M. Wilson's two duds since the Harrison trade are real and he is worth his ECR value (13.1 ppg).

The trade also moves bye-week pain around:
- It fixes Week 11 for Jamal (119 vs 102 lineup points).
- It wrecks Week 14, the last regular-season week, when Javonte, Pickens and M. Wilson are all on bye (110 vs 123).
- Tyson adds only about 3 pts all season.

The offer is open until Sat Oct 24 7:09 PM ET. The Rams' Friday final injury report and McVay's Friday comments have not been found yet, and they will matter more than anything modeled here.

Plan:
1. Message Daoud (rather than using ESPN's formal counter, which I believe declines the original offer — worth confirming) and ask for Javonte + M. Wilson + Isaiah Likely in place of Tyson. Likely is an extra idea outside the requested list. It is the only version that beats holding even with a healthy Nacua (+45 pts over Weeks 8-17, +4.6 per week in the playoffs), because TE is Jamal's weakest slot.
2. If Daoud says no, accept the original offer as sent if the Friday/Saturday news says Nacua is OUT for Week 7 with a strain, a multi-week timeline, an MRI finding, or any return of the groin/pre-hernia issue.
3. HOLD if Nacua is questionable or expected back by Week 8.

v.verdict:
As of Friday Oct 23, no source says how bad Nacua's calf injury is. It has not been shown to be minor (0-1 games missed) or serious. I ran 28 WebSearch queries; 26 returned results before the search budget ran out. The latest reporting is from Thursday Oct 22 (ESPN/Barshop, Schefter, Rapoport, PFT, CBS/RotoWire, Rotoworld, SI, AP/Yahoo). He left practice early with a calf injury, a team spokesperson confirmed it, and he was officially LIMITED, not DNP. PFT said there was 'no immediate word on the seriousness.' No MRI or imaging result, no McVay quote about the calf, no Friday practice line and no Week 7 designation turned up. Early Week 7 reads were 'highly questionable' (Rotoworld), 'very questionable' (SI) and 'questionable at best' (The Big Lead, a guess). Nothing reported points to a serious injury, and the base rate for a WR calf strain is about 1.8 weeks missed (4for4, 2017-2021 data). The most likely outcome is that he is back by Week 8 or Week 9.

The center of the model's timeline (45% back by Week 8) holds up, but the rest leans too long. The mean of 2.41 weeks is above the benchmark. The 10% chance of 6+ weeks comes from the groin/pre-hernia history, which no source connects to the calf, and that tail supplies 46% of the +16.5 edge. The 'most likely' label actually names a weighted average. With benchmark weights the edge for (a) falls to about +9.7 at base and about -9.3 with M. Wilson at his ECR value. Adding a return-week production dip would win back about 3-4 points.

If he is back by Week 8, which is the single most likely outcome, taking the offer means selling low: -1.9 points at base and about -21 to -31 with M. Wilson at a realistic 12-13 ppg. The model's recommendation to wait is right. Its accept trigger ('OUT for Week 7 with a strain') is too loose, because by the model's own numbers a Week 7-only absence still loses. The trade becomes favorable only on credible news that he will miss Week 8 or longer.

Assessment of the three incoming players as of Fri Oct 23, 2026 (36 WebSearch queries).

JAVONTE WILLIAMS (DAL): Healthy. No 2026 injury report found. Dallas plays at PHI on Monday night Oct 26, so he is available for Week 7. A Razzball page claiming a Week 7 bye is contradicted by the official schedule. Dallas's bye is Week 14, the last week of this league's regular season. He is the clear workhorse: 85% snap share in Week 5, 91 touches and 7 TDs through 5 games, PPR RB7 as of Oct 15. He reportedly owns the goal-line work. Dallas cut Jaydon Blue and Mafah, and Malik Davis is on IR, so competition is minimal: Goodson, Demercado and Luepke combined for 19 touches through Week 5. Weekly line:
- W1: 12-41-1 rushing, 5/5 targets for 31 yds and a TD
- W3: 19-98-1
- W4: 3 rush TDs (62 carries, 231 yds, 5 TD through W4)
- W5: 14 touches, 62 yds, 1 TD
- W6: 11-41-1 rushing, 2/2 receiving for 9 yds

Concerns: efficiency is down (3.73 YPC), touches have fallen to 14 and 13 in Weeks 5-6, and Dallas is 2-4, held under 20 points for two straight games, which makes game scripts negative. Dak Prescott is starting with no injury found.

JORDYN TYSON (NO): On IR since Aug 30 (right hamstring, hurt Aug 13). He carries the designate-to-return tag, but no report shows his 21-day practice window opening. Around Oct 12, Moore said 'Not right now' about practicing. This week he is not practicing and is out for the Paris game vs PIT (Rotowire, Yahoo, BVM Sports Oct 21). The Saints are on bye in Week 8. Week 9 vs CLE is the earliest projected debut, but that is an analyst projection, not a team statement. He has a history of hamstring recurrences. Once healthy he is expected to start opposite Olave, with Vele (currently WR2) losing work.

MICHAEL WILSON (ARI): Healthy, with no injury designation this season. Week 7 is at home vs DEN. Marvin Harrison Jr. was traded to Houston around Oct 10, leaving Wilson the nominal WR1. Through 5 games he had 51 targets (tied 3rd in the NFL), but only 288 yds and 1 TD (WR24 half-PPR). He then went 4/7 for 30 yds (W5) and 4/7 for 32 yds (W6), outproduced in Week 6 by McBride and Bourne. RotoBaller still projects him as a mid-to-low WR2. The QB is Jacoby Brissett, with rookie Carson Beck (back issue) behind him. Arizona's bye is also Week 14.

Caveat: an SI piece with '23 targets through six weeks vs Harrison 34 / McBride 53' appears to be from 2025 and was excluded. Nothing here covers Puka Nacua's injury, which was outside this task.

counters.summary:
I ran about 29 web searches. Of Daoud's 9 players, the counter-offer news is:

- **Terry McLaurin is done for the season.** He tore his left patellar tendon on MNF Oct 19, and Washington confirmed it Oct 20. Don't ask for him.
- **Lamar Jackson is back at practice but not cleared.** He was limited Wed and Thu (Oct 21-22) after his Week 4 ankle sprain and was seen limping afterward. He is not on IR. His Friday designation wasn't found and his Week 7 status is uncertain.
- **Saquon Barkley is close to returning.** He missed Weeks 5-6 with a hamstring injury and was limited Thu Oct 22. Garafolo reports he is 'in line to play' Mon Oct 26 vs Dallas. Eagles trade rumors about him are speculation only.
- **James Cook is healthy but on bye in Week 7.** He had 153 total yards in Week 6 and has 716 scrimmage yards in 6 games. He's back Nov 1.
- **Chris Olave is healthy.** An illness had him questionable for Week 6, but he played (4 catches, 43 yards, 1 TD). He isn't on the Week 7 Wed/Thu reports I found. The Saints play in Paris on Sunday.
- **Chris Godwin Jr. is losing his role.** He has no TD this year and NBC calls him a WR4. He missed Thursday's practice on a rest day, not for an injury. Egbuka is in concussion protocol, which might mean more targets for Godwin.
- **Blake Corum is healthy and in a backup role.** He gets about 28-31% of the Rams backfield work but has scored in back-to-back games. He's a Week 7 flex/streamer option.
- **KC Concepcion has a new calf/quad injury.** He was limited Wed and Thu and is listed questionable at Tennessee. He returned from a Week 5 concussion to play Week 6.
- **Isaiah Likely is producing well.** He's the top half-PPR TE per RotoBaller with no current injury. His QB changes to J.J. McCarthy (Dart on IR, Winston benched).

**Benchings:** none among the 9 players; the only one in this research is Giants QB Winston, which affects Likely.

**Trades:** none of the 9 has been traded.

Context outside the 9: Puka Nacua left Thursday's practice early with a calf injury and was listed limited. McVay's Friday update wasn't found, and Davante Adams is on IR. Marvin Harrison Jr. was traded from ARI to HOU on Oct 12, which may matter for Michael Wilson. The trade deadline is Nov 10.

For counter-offer value, the healthy, productive targets are Likely, Olave, and Cook (after his bye), with Barkley a near-term return. McLaurin has no value, and Godwin's value is low. Some search results were really 2025 articles (a McLaurin quad injury, a Barkley Week 7 exit vs the Vikings, a Godwin fibula injury vs the Lions), and I left those out.
